client_brief:
Shoulder-season hospitality campaign built from carefully matched photography

Marisol Cove needs a shoulder-season campaign that reflects the light we actually have. Most of the coastal pictures will be licensed; the usable room photographs are ours. Our insurer does not allow generated or AI-made pictures in any piece of this campaign. The work is to make them belong together, not to promise a different coast or a different property.

Please prepare
- Shoulder-season key visual: 1 named export. The pictured property is correctly identified, and the Marisol Cove wordmark sits directly above the tagline. The tagline is exactly “The quiet side of the coast.” No date, discount or unlisted amenity is added.
- Hospitality booking story: 1 named export. The booking action, a line inviting guests to book by the phone number, email or web address printed on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf, stays inside the safe area.
- Seasonal offer card: 10 named exports. The words “Shoulder Rate” appear beside the supplied Shoulder Rate value and “Winter Rate” beside the Winter Rate value, with the room name, sleeps, minimum stay and Includes line from marisol_rates_autumn.csv. The property identity, the Marisol Cove wordmark, is visible.
- Seasonal hospitality brochure: 1 named export. The offer is understandable without the original brief: it gives each room's name, sleeps, Shoulder Rate, Winter Rate and minimum stay from marisol_rates_autumn.csv, and the cancellation terms from marisol_copy.md. The property imagery is truthful.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: The quiet side of the coast.
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen room boutique hotel on the bluff above a cove, selling nights and the dining room to couples and small groups.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, on the Mendocino coast of Northern California, run by two owners with nine staff.
brand_identity.about: Marisol Cove is a small clifftop hotel built around a path down to a private beach and a dining room people plan a trip for. There is no pool and no spa, and the point of the place is the light, the water and being left alone. The autumn and winter shoulder season is the first the owners are pushing properly.
brand_identity.audience: Couples and small groups aged 30 to 55, experience led rather than amenity led, who book for the setting and the food and return in the quiet months.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Rooms run 340 to 620 dollars a night. Boutique premium, above a coastal inn and well below a resort or private estate. The rate is carried by the setting, not by facilities.

palette.name: Bluff Sand
palette.role: mandatory as the ground of every offer card and brochure page and of any text panel
palette.usage: The solid ground of every offer card and brochure page, as on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf, and of any text panel on the key visual or booking story; also type set directly on a dark area of a photograph.

palette.name: Cove Grey Blue
palette.usage: The hairline rules beneath headlines and the tagline, and a decorative wave rule such as the one above the footer of marisol_rate_card_press.pdf. Never the wordmark's own wave rule, which takes the colour of its letters. Never type: that card's Cove Grey Blue rate lines break the rule that a rate is never coloured. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Cypress
palette.usage: Small labels only, such as a sleeps line, an INCLUDES label or the contact line, as on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf. Never a rate, headline, room name, ground or panel.

palette.name: Warm Ink
palette.role: mandatory on Bluff Sand for the wordmark and its wave rule, headlines, room names, body text, rates and captions
palette.usage: On Bluff Sand: the wordmark and its wave rule in one ink, as painted on marisol_sign_photo.jpg, and headlines, room names, body text, rates and captions, as the room name and Includes text are on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Dusk Clay
palette.usage: Thin keylines only, as on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf. Never type, a ground or a panel.

brand_identity.typography: Marisol Cove runs four steps. Step 01, display, is Urbanist Light small caps at 36 pt on 40 pt leading tracked to 240 units, with a single 0.4 pt hairline rule beneath trimmed to the exact width of that tracked line; the key visual sets the same row at 88 px on 96 px and the tagline at 34 px on 42 px, each with its own width matched hairline. Step 02, subheading, is Freight Sans Pro Medium at 16 pt on 22 pt with +60 tracking, used for room names only and never given the 240 tracking or the hairline. Step 03, body, is Freight Sans Pro Book at 10 pt on 16 pt with tracking 0 to a maximum of 65 characters, and the body is never tracked. Step 04, fine print, is Freight Sans Pro Book at 8 pt on 12 pt with +20 tracking for rates and captions, with figures left in Book weight.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, plain and specific. It describes what is actually there and lets the reader picture it. Example line the brand would write: An hour before sunset the light comes off the water and the whole cove goes gold. That is when to walk down.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The logo file was lost with the designer who drew it in 2019. The mark, a small caps wordmark over a hairline wave rule, survives only as the painted sign at the entrance, which the owners have photographed. Room photography is the owners' own phone frames plus licensed stock. No usable brand files remain beyond the sign photo.
brand_identity.values: One place under one light. Every guest facing piece should read as the same specific cove, honest about a fourteen room hotel rather than dressed up as something grander.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The wordmark and every headline are Urbanist Light small caps tracked to 240 units, with a single 0.4 pt hairline rule cut to the exact width of the tracked line sitting beneath it.

type_system.tagline: The quiet side of the coast.
type_system.text_face: Freight Sans Pro Book, Medium for room names

scale.sample: THE QUIET SIDE OF THE COAST
scale.note: Wordmark and every headline. A single 0.4 pt hairline rule sits beneath, trimmed to the exact width of the tracked line and never to the column. On the key visual the same row runs 88 px on 96 px, with the tagline below it at 34 px on 42 px, both at the same 240 tracking and each with its own width matched hairline.
Room names only. Medium appears nowhere else, and this step never takes the 240 tracking or the hairline rule, both of which belong to the display line.

scale.sample: An hour before sunset the light comes off the water.
scale.note: The open 16 pt leading against a 10 pt size is what keeps the page quiet. Never track the body.

scale.sample: Marisol Cove, on the Mendocino coast.
scale.note: Rates and captions. Figures stay Book weight and are never emboldened or coloured to draw the eye.

type_system.signature_move: The tracking. The wordmark and every headline are Urbanist Light small caps at 240 units, wide enough that each letter reads as a separate mark, with one 0.4 pt hairline rule cut to the exact width of the tracked line sitting beneath it. At brochure size that is 36 pt on 40 pt, on the key visual 88 px on 96 px with the 34 px tagline below, and the long thin band of spaced capitals over its width matched hairline is what a guest recognises first.
rules: The wordmark and every headline are small caps tracked to 240 units, and nothing else is ever tracked that wide.
The hairline rule is always 0.4 pt and always trimmed to the exact width of the tracked line above it, never to the column width.
Urbanist Light is the only display weight. Freight Sans Pro Medium is reserved for room names, Book sets body, rates and captions.
Rates are set in the same Book weight as the body. Never colour or embolden a rate.
Every guest facing piece reads as the same specific cove, honest about a fourteen room hotel rather than dressed up as something grander.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Bluff Sand and nothing else, as on marisol_rate_card_press.pdf. On Bluff Sand, the wordmark, headlines, room names, body text, rates and captions are Warm Ink, and a rate is never given a colour of its own. Cypress sets small labels only (a sleeps line, an INCLUDES label, the contact line). The wave rule beneath the wordmark takes the colour of its letters, as marisol_sign_photo.jpg paints both in one ink. Cove Grey Blue is for the hairline rules beneath headlines and the tagline and for a decorative wave rule such as the one above the footer of marisol_rate_card_press.pdf; Dusk Clay is for thin keylines. Type set directly on a photograph is Warm Ink or Bluff Sand. Cypress, Cove Grey Blue and Dusk Clay together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity; no tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode; no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, laid over a photograph: a text panel sits over or beside the photograph as a solid Bluff Sand block.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; no colour and no bold on a rate, which stays Warm Ink in the body's Book weight; no burst badge or savings callout, as the plain marisol_rate_card_press.pdf card has none.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette: no Bluff Sand, Cove Grey Blue or Dusk Clay wash over a frame, and the cove's water and sky are not pushed toward Cove Grey Blue. A colour that belongs to the room, such as a painted wall, stays that colour when a cast is corrected.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve approved copy, dimensions, hierarchy, and reproduction requirements; do not imply a data merge or editable system that is outside the scoped deliverables.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
